1) Load Data and Data Cleaning¶

In [2]:
df = pd.read_csv('tfrrs_all_distance_events_one_csv.csv').copy()

def time_to_seconds(value):
    if pd.isna(value):
        return np.nan
    s = str(value).strip().replace('@', '').replace('*', '')
    if not s:
        return np.nan
    parts = s.split(':')
    try:
        if len(parts) == 1:
            return float(parts[0])
        if len(parts) == 2:
            return int(parts[0]) * 60 + float(parts[1])
        if len(parts) == 3:
            return int(parts[0]) * 3600 + int(parts[1]) * 60 + float(parts[2])
    except ValueError:
        return np.nan
    return np.nan

def seconds_to_clock(x, pos=None):
    if pd.isna(x):
        return ''
    t = int(round(max(float(x), 0.0)))
    h, rem = divmod(t, 3600)
    m, s = divmod(rem, 60)
    if h > 0:
        return f'{h}:{m:02d}:{s:02d}'
    return f'{m}:{s:02d}'

df['Date_dt'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Date'], errors='coerce')
df['Year_num'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Year'], errors='coerce')
df['Month_num'] = df['Date_dt'].dt.month
df['Month_name'] = pd.Categorical(
    df['Date_dt'].dt.strftime('%b'),
    categories=['Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun','Jul','Aug','Sep','Oct','Nov','Dec'],
    ordered=True
)
df['Performance_Seconds'] = df['Performance Time'].apply(time_to_seconds)

# 2021 is often sparse/partial in this scrape history, so remove it for cleaner comparisons.
df = df[df['Year_num'] != 2021].copy()

print(f'Rows: {len(df):,}')

In [5]:
monthly = (
    df.dropna(subset=['Date_dt'])
      .groupby(['Year_num', 'Month_name'], as_index=False)
      .size()
      .rename(columns={'size': 'Entries'})
)

plt.figure(figsize=(15, 6))
sns.lineplot(data=monthly, x='Month_name', y='Entries', hue='Year_num', marker='o', linewidth=2)
plt.title('Monthly Entry Patterns by Year')
plt.xlabel('Month')
plt.ylabel('Entries')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Analysis¶

  • This makes sense. The indoor season peaks in Feb with conference in March, so there will be less entries.
  • Outdoor season peaks in Apr with conference in May. There are some meets in December.

Analysis¶

  • Visually it appears from this the average time is increasing from freshman to senior year. THis is a good example of selection bias. As athletes get older they enter into longer events, so that is why the median time is increasing.

5) By Event¶

Side-by-side event distribution comparisons by gender.

In [23]:
events = ['1500m', 'mile', '3k', '5k', '10k']
class_order = ['FR', 'SO', 'JR', 'SR']
class_palette = {'FR': '#4C78A8', 'SO': '#F58518', 'JR': '#54A24B', 'SR': '#E45756'}

for event_name in events:
    event_df = perf[perf['Event'] == event_name].copy()
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(18, 6), sharex=False, sharey=False)
    fig.suptitle(f'{event_name}: Class Distributions on Shared Axes', fontsize=18, y=1.03)

    for ax, gender in zip(axes, ['Male', 'Female']):
        gender_df = event_df[event_df['Gender'] == gender]

        for class_name in class_order:
            subset = gender_df[gender_df['Class'] == class_name]['Performance_Seconds'].dropna()
            if len(subset) == 0:
                continue

            sns.histplot(
                subset,
                bins=50,
                stat='density',
                element='step',
                fill=True,
                alpha=0.22,
                kde=True,
                color=class_palette[class_name],
                label=f'{class_name} (n={len(subset)})',
                ax=ax,
            )

        ax.set_title(f'{gender}')
        ax.set_xlabel('Time')
        ax.set_ylabel('Density')
        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(seconds_to_clock))
        ax.legend(title='Class')

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

Analysis¶

  • The junior and seniors are much more sucessful in the 10k distance for male and females
  • 10k is the only event with more seniors in both men/women have more observations

6) Key Findings & Summary¶

-Entries peak sharply in February (Indoor Conference) and April/May (Outdoor Conference). The drop-off in March is a clear indicator of the transition period between the two seasons.

  • 1500m and 5k by far have the most entries.
  • It looks like athletes are getting slower as they age (median times increasing from FR to SR), this is a result of selection bias
    • Seniors are significantly more likely to compete in the 10k, whereas Freshmen are concentrated in the 1500m, this event change pulls the median performance time up for older athletes.
